source_text:
ἀνθρώπων γεγόνασιν, ὅτι πατοῦνται, ὅτι ὑπ' αὐτῶν ἐμπαίζονται ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ
κυρίου. ἄλλοι δὲ τὸ ἀπεκδυσάμενος ἀντὶ τοῦ ἐκδύσας ἐξέλαβον. 323,col2 Τὸ καθ'
ἡμῶν δὲ χειρόγραφον πῶς ἐξήλειψεν; ὅτε ἐδόθη ὁ νόμος ὁ καταρώμενος τοὺς
παραβαίνοντας, πᾶς ὁ λαὸς Ἰσραὴλ ἐπεβόησεν δεχόμενος καὶ συντιθέμενος· ὥσπερ
οὖν χειρόγραφον ἡ συγκατάθεσις γέγονεν. τοῦτο οὖν τὸ χειρόγραφον ἐξήλειψε τοῖς
δόγμασιν. ποίοις; τοῖς ἀπαλλάττουσι μὲν τῆς κατὰ νόμον πολιτείας, παρέχουσι δὲ
τὴν ἐν χάριτι πολιτείαν. Ἐπειδὴ ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἐπολιτεύσατο, τὴν παρακοὴν λύων καὶ
τὴν 324,col2 ἁμαρτίαν ἀναιρῶν, προσηνέχθη καὶ τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν ἐβάστασεν.
ταύτας δὲ ἀπολλὺς καθεῖλε τὴν δύναμιν τὴν διαβολικήν, ἀντὶ τοῦ εἰπεῖν ἐκδύσας
τὰς ἀρχὰς καὶ τὰς ἐξουσίας ἐδειγμάτισεν ἀπεκδυσάμενος, καὶ διὰ ταύτης τῆς
ἐκδύσεως θριαμβεύσας καὶ παραδειγματίσας τὰς ἀντικειμένας δυνάμεις. ἐν ἑαυτῷ
οὖν ἐκείνας ἀπεξεδύσατο, καὶ ἐκείνας ἐθριάμβευσεν δι' ὧν ἔπαθεν καὶ κατώρθωσεν.
Kol 2,16–18α Μὴ οὖν τις ὑμᾶς κρινέτω. διδάσκει ὅτι ὁ νόμος κατήργηται,
ἐξαλείψαντος τὸ καθ' ἡμῶν χειρόγραφον τοῦ Χριστοῦ. διδάσκει δὲ ὅτι καὶ ὁ πονηρὸς
καταπέπτωκεν ἀπεκδυσαμένου τοῦ κυρίου καὶ παραδειγματίσαντος τὰς ἀρχὰς καὶ
τὰς ἐξουσίας. παραγγέλλει λοιπὸν μηκέτι τούτοις ὑπακούειν τοῖς καταργηθεῖσι διὰ
τῆς τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐνεργείας· ὥστε μήτε Ἰουδαίοις, φησίν, ἀναπείθουσιν ὑμᾶς
φυλάττειν τὰ ἐν τῷ νόμῳ ὑπάγεσθε. σκιὰ γὰρ ἦν ἐκεῖνα τοῦ σώματος τοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὅ
ἐστιν ἡ ἐκκλησία. ἡ δὲ σκιὰ προτρέχει μὲν τοῦ σώματος, ὑπό325 στασιν δὲ δι' ἑαυτῆς
οὐκ ἔχει. διό φησιν· νόμῳ μὴ ὑπακούετε. ἀλλὰ μὴν μηδὲ Ἕλλησι μετάγουσιν ὑμᾶς
εἰς τὸ προσκυνεῖν ἀγγέλοις ἢ τοῖς στοιχείοις τοῦ κόσμου τούτου· ἐμβατεύουσι γὰρ ἃ
μὴ ἑωράκασιν ἀπ' ἰδίου νοὸς καὶ ἀπ' ἰδίου λογισμοῦ καθαιρόμενοι. τὸ οὖν μή τις
ὑμᾶς κρινέτω περὶ Ἰουδαίων εἴρηται, τὸ δὲ μή τις ὑμᾶς καταβραβευέτω περὶ
Ἑλλήνων. φησὶ δέ· μηδεὶς ὑμῖν ἐπιβουλευέτω νικῶσιν ἤδη καὶ καταγωνιζομένοις
τὸν πονηρόν. 324,col2 Ἅ ἐστι σκιὰ τῶν μελλόντων, τὸ δὲ σῶμα Χριστοῦ. 325,col2 ὅτε
pass_a_gloss:
[continuing the Colossians 2:14-15 note] ... human beings, that they are trampled on, that they are mocked by them in the name of the Lord. And others took "having stripped off (from himself)" in place of "having stripped (them)."
[Second catena form, 323-324 col. 2:] And how did he wipe out the bond against us? When the law that curses those who transgress was given, all the people of Israel shouted out, accepting and agreeing; so the assent became like a handwritten bond. This bond, then, he wiped out by the decrees. Which ones? Those that release from the way of life according to the law and provide the way of life in grace. Since he lived his life for us, undoing the disobedience and doing away with the sin, he was offered and bore our sins. And destroying these he brought down the devilish power; in place of saying "having stripped the rulers and the authorities," he made a show of them "having stripped off," and through this stripping off having triumphed over and made an example of the opposing powers. So in himself he stripped those off, and he triumphed over those through the things he suffered and accomplished.
Colossians 2:16-18a. "So let no one judge you." He teaches that the law has been abolished, Christ having wiped out the bond against us. And he teaches that the evil one too has fallen, the Lord having stripped off and made an example of the rulers and the authorities. He commands, then, no longer to obey these things abolished through the working of Christ; so neither, he says, be led on by Jews who try to persuade you to keep the things in the law. For those things were a shadow of the body of Christ, which is the church. And the shadow runs ahead of the body, but has no substance through itself. Therefore he says: do not obey the law. But neither indeed (be led on by) Greeks who carry you over to worshipping angels or the elements of this world; for they step into things they have not seen, being purified from their own mind and from their own reasoning. So "let no one judge you" is said about the Jews, and "let no one disqualify you" about the Greeks. And he says: let no one plot against you, who are already conquering and overcoming the evil one.
[Second catena form, 324-325 col. 2:] "Which are a shadow of the things to come, but the body is of Christ." When [continues in the next section]
pass_b_english: … human beings: they are trampled underfoot, and human beings mock them in the name of the Lord. Others took “having stripped off” in the sense of “having stripped them”.

The second catena form adds: … He wiped out this bond by his decrees. Which decrees? Those that set us free from life under the law and give us the life of grace. Since he lived his life for our sake, undoing the disobedience and doing away with sin, he was offered up and bore our sins (Hebrews 9:28). By destroying our sins he brought down the devil’s power. Instead of saying “having stripped the rulers and authorities”, he says “having stripped off, he made a public show of them”; and by this stripping off he triumphed over the opposing powers and made an example of them. So in himself he stripped them off, and he triumphed over them through what he suffered and what he achieved.

On Colossians 2:16–18: “So let no one judge you.” He teaches that the law has been abolished, now that Christ has wiped out the bond that stood against us. He teaches too that the evil one has fallen, now that the Lord has stripped off the rulers and authorities and made an example of them. So he tells them not to obey any longer these things that Christ’s working has abolished. Do not, he says, be won over by Jews who try to persuade you to keep what is in the law. Those things were a shadow of the body of Christ, which is the church. A shadow runs ahead of the body, but it has no substance of its own. That is why he says: do not obey the law. And do not be won over by Greeks who draw you into worshipping angels or the elements of this world either; for they “intrude into things they have not seen”, seeking purification from their own mind and their own reasoning. So “let no one judge you” is said about the Jews, and “let no one rob you of the prize” about the Greeks. He means: let no one plot against you, now that you are already winning and getting the better of the evil one.
The second catena form adds: “Which are a shadow of the things to come, but the body is Christ’s” (Colossians 2:17).

choices.term: ἄλλοι δὲ τὸ ἀπεκδυσάμενος ἀντὶ τοῦ ἐκδύσας ἐξέλαβον
choices.english: Others took “having stripped off” in the sense of “having stripped them”.
choices.why: The contrast is middle (stripping off from himself) against active (stripping the powers); the old English gave both the same English ('having stripped off' instead of 'having stripped off').
rejected: Others took 'having stripped off' instead of 'having stripped off'

choices.term: 323,col2 Τὸ καθ' ἡμῶν δὲ χειρόγραφον πῶς ἐξήλειψεν; … δι' ὧν ἔπαθεν καὶ κατώρθωσεν.
choices.english: Doublet collapsed (Colossians 2:14–15): first form kept in u01-rem-close; this second form reduced to 'The second catena form adds:'
choices.why: The account of Israel's assent becoming a bond repeats the first form and is not reprinted. Added material kept: which decrees (those that free from the law's way of life and give grace's), 'he was offered and bore our sins', destroying sin brought down the devil's power, the middle-for-active remark, and 'in himself he stripped them off'.
rejected: How did the handwriting that was against us erase itself? (old)

choices.why: The note covers 2:16 ('let no one judge you'), 2:17 (shadow and body) and 2:18 ('let no one rob you of the prize', 'intruding into what they have not seen'). The old English printed '(Col 2:16-18a)' after 2:16 and '(Col 2:18)' after the words of 2:17 (SOURCE_ISSUES item 2).

choices.term: ἀπ' ἰδίου νοὸς καὶ ἀπ' ἰδίου λογισμοῦ καθαιρόμενοι
choices.english: seeking purification from their own mind and their own reasoning
choices.why: καθαίρω middle/passive 'purify (oneself)'; Severian seems to point to Greek purification teaching. Uncertain (the verse itself has 'puffed up by the mind of his flesh'); recorded in translator_notes.

choices.term: 324,col2 Ἅ ἐστι σκιὰ … 325,col2 ὅτε | ἐγένετο ταῦτα …
choices.english: The second catena form adds: “Which are a shadow of the things to come, but the body is Christ’s” (Colossians 2:17).
choices.why: Second catena form of the shadow note. Its first sentence ('when these things happened they were a shadow ... the shadow runs ahead of the body') repeats the first form and is not printed; the section ends cleanly after the lemma, and its new sentences are printed at the start of u02-rem-early after '…'.
rejected: That which is a shadow of the things to come, but the body is Christ (Col 2:18) (old)
